summary: A proposal by Jon Postel that willing hosts run an Echo process for debugging and measurement. It listens for a connection, completes the Initial Connection Protocol, and sends back whatever data arrives, bit for bit. The connection ends when it is closed. BBN-TENEX already offered such a process.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC suggests an Echo process for testing and measuring network connections. It returns received data unchanged so a sender can compare what it sent with what came back.

subtitle: A suggested service that returns received data unchanged for debugging and measurement.

tldr.problem: Hosts could use a simple service for debugging and network measurement.
tldr.mechanism: A willing host accepts a connection using ICP and sends each received data block back bit for bit without modification.
tldr.outcome: The RFC suggests that hosts implement the process voluntarily and notes that BBN-TENEX already had one.

sections.title: A Voluntary Echo Service
sections.content: Jon Postel suggests that hosts willing to do so implement an Echo process for debugging and measurement. The proposal does not require every host to offer the service.
sections.plainLanguage: Hosts are invited, but not required, to provide an Echo process. The stated uses are debugging and measurement.

sections.title: How Echo Works
sections.content:
The process listens for a connection and performs the Initial Connection Protocol (ICP) described in the Current Network Protocols notebook. After ICP completes, it waits for data from the network.

When data arrives, the process sends it back immediately, bit for bit, without modification, and reallocates buffer space. It ends when the network connections are closed.
sections.plainLanguage: The process establishes a connection, waits for data and sends that data back unchanged. Closing the network connections ends the process.

sections.title: Existing Example
sections.content: The RFC notes that BBN-TENEX had offered an Echo process for a long time. It gives no other host implementation requirements.
sections.plainLanguage: BBN-TENEX is named as an existing example. The suggestion remains voluntary for other hosts.
